question: _________ is a significant festival of the Parsi people who practice Zoroastrianism as it marks the birth anniversary of Zoroaster.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Khordad Sal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khordad Sal** is a significant festival celebrated by the Parsi community, who practice Zoroastrianism.
 
• This festival marks the birth anniversary of **Zoroaster**, the founder of Zoroastrianism.
 
• It is a day of thanksgiving and celebration, where Parsis engage in prayers, feasting, and community activities.
 
• The festival is observed with great fervor and is considered one of the most important events in the Zoroastrian calendar.
 
• On this day, Zoroastrians reflect on the teachings of Zoroaster and reaffirm their commitment to the principles of good thoughts, good words, and good deeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoroastrianism** is one of the world's oldest monotheistic religions, dating back to the 6th century BCE in ancient Persia.
 
• The religion emphasizes the duality of good and evil and the importance of individual choice in promoting good.
 
• Zoroaster, also known as Zarathustra, is considered a prophet and a spiritual leader who reformed the ancient religious practices of Persia.
 
• The Parsi community in India is one of the largest groups of Zoroastrians globally, having migrated from Persia to avoid religious persecution.
 
• Other important festivals for Zoroastrians include **Jamshed-e-Navroz** (the Persian New Year) and **Pateti** (the last day of the Zoroastrian year).
